articles.title: New wildfire in Southern California explodes in size, burning multiple homes
articles.summary: A fast-moving wildfire in Southern California quickly consumed hundreds of acres and burned multiple homes after sparking in Orange County Friday, county off...
articles.body:
A fast-moving wildfire in Southern California quickly consumed hundreds of acres and burned multiple homes after sparking in Orange County Friday, county officials said.

The Norte Fire began around noon near a neighborhood in the San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano areas and by Friday evening had grown to 570 acres, the Orange County Fire Authority said. It's one of several fires that have broken out since Thursday amid fierce Santa Ana winds affecting Southern California.

"Our actions today will be to continue to attack the fire and work toward getting residents home as soon as it's safe to so do," Orange County Fire Authority Captain Greg Barta said Saturday morning in a video on X .

Topography and weather conditions allowed the fire to grow rapidly, Orange County Division 3 Fire Chief Mark Backoff said in a video posted to social media Friday afternoon.

Six homes have been destroyed or damaged by the fire, and two firefighters suffered "significant" injuries but are stable in area hospitals, fire officials said.

Evacuation orders were issued for multiple areas in San Clemente and San Juan Capistrano, encompassing roughly 4,600 homes and 16,000 people, Orange County Fire Authority Chief TJ McGovern said. Officials asked residents to be patient as they evaluate when it will be safe to return home.

Officials said progress had been made against the fire by the evening but warned conditions remained volatile.

"A majority of the fire has been knocked down. However, we still have some homes that have been impacted here, and as you can see, the wind is still blowing pretty strong up here," Orange County Fire Authority spokesperson Steve Concialdi said.

The fire is now 5% contained as of Saturday morning. Crews' objective is "keeping the fire within its current footprint," McGovern said at a news conference Friday evening.

Aerial footage from CNN affiliate KCBS showed multiple houses burning Friday afternoon.

Resident Robert Morris called the sudden threat to homes "a wake-up call," telling KCBS, "I've lived here since 1995, and this is the first time we've really ever had a fire in this area."

US Rep. Mike Levin, a Democrat whose district includes part of Orange County, said his family had to evacuate their San Juan Capistrano home while he attended an event nearby.

Levin thanked firefighters for preventing greater damage from the fire and said "year-round wildfire season" has become the "new normal" for Southern California.

Orange County sheriff's deputies were going door to door in areas under evacuation order, telling people to leave for their safety, Sgt. Lizbeth Gwisdalla, a spokesperson for the sheriff's department, told CNN.

Ten schools were dismissed early "out of an abundance of caution" and sports and after-school programs were canceled, Capistrano Unified School District announced .

Wind gusts in the area reached 25 mph Friday afternoon and remained elevated into the evening. The Santa Ana winds had eased to gusts of 17 mph by Saturday and are expected to diminish later in the weekend.

"We're going to be here for a number of days," Concialdi said of the ongoing danger, stressing the need to guard against new fires that could erupt from embers blown by the strong Santa Ana winds.

Several fires have broken out since Santa Ana winds began Thursday, forcing evacuations in other areas of Southern California.

In Malibu, more than 7,000 structures were in areas under evacuation orders or warnings on Friday because of the Bryson Fire, which has burned roughly 150 acres and is 52% contained since starting Thursday evening, a Los Angeles County Fire spokesperson told CNN, estimating the number of people under evacuation orders to be in the hundreds.

Crews made "great progress" against the fire overnight, Los Angeles County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said during a news conference Friday morning.

At least one firefighter had "minor injuries" and was taken to the hospital, he said. The chief did not provide additional details except to say, "They've been on the line all night, so minor injuries are expected."

The fire is still threatening more than 100 structures in the area, but no damages have been reported. "But obviously, if the winds kick up later this afternoon and we were to lose containment of the fire, a larger area could be affected and under threat," the chief said. Over 400 firefighters and more than 75 "ground and aerial resources" are committed to the Bryson Fire, he said.

Another wildfire to the south has burned more than 3,000 acres near the Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton since igniting Thursday afternoon, according to the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection ( Cal Fire ).

The Henderson Fire forced a temporary evacuation order for one area of the base Thursday and the closure of a nearby portion of Interstate 5 in San Diego County, the Marine Corps said in a statement Friday. Smoke affected visibility along both sides of the highway Friday afternoon, the California Highway Patrol said. The fire is 35% contained as of Saturday morning, according to Cal Fire .

The Camp Pendleton Fire Department and Cal Fire continue to actively fight the fire, but it was burning "in a remote section" of the base and there were no active threats to personnel or facilities, the Marine Corps statement Friday said.

The dangerous fire conditions in Southern California have also prompted utility companies to temporarily shut off power for tens of thousands over concerns that equipment could spark fires.

This story has been updated with additional information.

Meteorologist Chris Dolce and CNN's Kate S. Petersen and Isa Mudannayake contributed to this report.

articles.title: In 1968, millions of grey squirrels moved across America in a puzzling wildlife event, and scientists traced a possible clue to the acorn crop of 1967
articles.summary: In the autumn of 1968, reports of eastern grey squirrels moving in unusual numbers across parts of the northeastern United States drew attention to a
articles.body: In the autumn of 1968, reports of eastern grey squirrels moving in unusual numbers across parts of the northeastern United States drew attention to a puzzling wildlife event. The scale of the movement was striking, but the animals had not necessarily begun travelling without reason. Their behaviour may have reflected changes in the food supply that had taken place over several seasons. Acorns, a major source of food for squirrels, vary considerably in abundance from one year to the next. When a good harvest is followed by a poor one, animals that have benefited from plentiful food can suddenly face a very different landscape. The weather in the preceding year may help explain how that imbalance developed.The mystery behind the 1968 eastern grey squirrel migrationEastern grey squirrels (Sciurus carolinensis) depend on a varied diet, but acorns are an important part of their food supply in oak woodland. The number of acorns produced by trees can fluctuate sharply between years. A forest that provides abundant food one autumn may offer much less the next, leaving squirrels with fewer resources just as their numbers may have increased.Some estimates put the number of squirrels involved in the 1968 irruption at 20 million, according to Smithsonian magazine. The unusual movement occurred across parts of the eastern United States, particularly the Appalachian region, where squirrels were reported crossing highways, entering buildings and attempting to swim across lakes and reservoirs.What happened to the acorn crop before the migrationThe study published in Forest Ecology and Management, titled ‘A perfect storm: Weather variability, mast failure, and the 1968 gray squirrel irruption in the eastern US’, investigate the possible causes, scientists examined oak seed production in the Asheville region of North Carolina, an area associated with the 1968 squirrel irruption. Their analysis covered 12 years, from 1962 to 1973, and included five oak species. They compared annual acorn production with temperature and rainfall during the growing season, looking for weather patterns that might help explain why some years produced plentiful crops while others did not.The findings pointed towards a complicated relationship between weather and tree reproduction. Warmer spring and summer conditions were associated with reduced acorn production in several of the species examined. The effects varied according to the type of oak and the stage of development, meaning that a single weather pattern did not affect every tree in the same way.Why the weather in 1967 attracted attentionThe scientists also examined whether the unusual weather associated with the North Carolina records could be detected across the wider northeastern United States. This helped establish whether the conditions affecting local oak production were part of a broader regional pattern rather than something confined to a small area.Some of the weather variables fell towards the extremes of the standard 1961–1990 climate reference period. Summer 1967 temperatures, in particular, stood out as the lowest in that record. This offered a possible clue to the unusual sequence of acorn harvests that preceded the following year's squirrel movement.The relationship was not as simple as saying that one cold summer caused millions of animals to migrate. Tree reproduction responds to conditions over different stages of development, and the effects of weather can carry over from one growing season to another. The study also found evidence that a large crop in one year could be followed by a smaller crop in the next, supporting the idea that trees may need time to replenish resources used during heavy seed production.How a plentiful harvest can contribute to a wildlife irruptionA large crop of acorns does more than feed the squirrels already living in a forest. Abundant food can improve survival and breeding opportunities, allowing more animals to persist in an area. Squirrels also store food for later use, but their caches cannot always compensate for a major shortfall in the following season.If food becomes scarce after a period of abundance, competition increases. Animals may travel further in search of suitable feeding grounds, move into unfamiliar habitats or appear in places where they are not normally seen in large numbers. articles.title: North Korea: What satellite images reveal about Kim Jong Un's summer retreat
articles.summary: Satellite images give clues about how Kim spends his holidays - something far out of reach for most North Koreans.
articles.body:
An 80m (263ft) luxury vessel has been repeatedly spotted in satellite images off North Korea's Wonsan coast from July to mid-October this year.

What stands out is the 50m swimming pool along the deck, with a cluster of waterslides at one end.

After sitting idle for months at a maintenance facility, it relocated in early July to waters off a strip of coastline known as the Kalma Peninsula.

This is close to Wonsan, a seaside resort with a sprawling villa used by North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and his family.

It was not the only large vessel on the move. A handful of others were also repeatedly seen near Kim's villa, in satellite images analysed by the BBC.

The vessels are widely believed to be used by Kim and his family. Former North Korean officials, defectors and experts say it would be difficult for anyone unconnected to the regime's leadership to own or freely use vessels of this size.

"In winter, they would keep them at the shipyard. When summer came, they would bring them out and move them to Kim Jong Un's villa or towards Kalma, and use them for swimming and recreation," says Ri Jong Ho.

Ri was once an official at the Workers' Party's Office 39, which is believed to be involved in raising and managing foreign currency for the leadership.

The wealth of those who sit at the top of the secretive North Korean dictatorship is just as hard to pin down as the country's economic figures.

The United Nations and others rely on estimates to classify North Korea as one of the world's poorest countries, with an especially large military budget that funds a sanctioned nuclear programme.

Most North Koreans, according to a 2025 UN report, live under "systematic, widespread and gross human rights violations" with total state control, widespread forced labour, and chronic food shortages that leave an estimated 40% of the population undernourished.

But the regime has long been known to live in luxury.

We don't know the cost of the vessels seen in the satellite imagery, but comparable luxury yachts run from tens of millions to over $100m (£75m). Kim's much smaller, 29-metre Princess yacht was previously estimated to be worth about $7m.

While vessel locations alone cannot definitively establish the family's whereabouts, their movements - which overlap with gaps in Kim's public appearances - point to activities that would otherwise remain out of public view.

Wonsan is where Kim Jong Un spent part of his childhood with his mother, according to biographers and intelligence reports, and one expert told the BBC the city has been associated with the family since his father Kim Jong Il's rule.

A defector who served for 13 years guarding residences used by then leader Kim Jong Il - through the 1990s to the early 2000s - told the BBC the villas around Wonsan were used as a retreat by the elite. He recalls seeing dozens of children and teens waterskiing during summer.

North Korean state media rarely publishes reports about Kim being on holiday, instead framing such visits as official inspections or guidance. But defectors interviewed by the BBC appeared to be aware that the family spent holidays in Wonsan, suggesting that at least some North Koreans knew about it.

North Korean state media also claims Wonsan is home to high-rise hotels, restaurants, shops, sports facilities and water parks, and can accommodate nearly 20,000 visitors.

State media and Russian outlets have published images of small groups of Russian tourists visiting the Wonsan Kalma resort, which opened in July 2025. Although developed to attract foreign visitors, the resort is also open to local tourists.

A South Korean news report, citing an unnamed source, says some locals were offered four-night tour packages for around $100, a substantial sum for most North Koreans. The country's per capita GDP - around $667 in 2024, according to the UN - is a small fraction of South Korea's $36,227.

For the majority of North Koreans, holidays are out of reach. And while a growing middle class does exist, they might not have much time for leisure.

Defectors told the BBC that workers, office employees and cooperative farmers are legally entitled to 14 days of annual leave, but this is rarely followed.

Taking consecutive days off to travel is unusual. People typically take weekend trips or travel during national holidays instead of designated "summer holidays".

Even if leave is granted, travel itself is restricted, with official permission required for people to travel outside their city or county. Moving freely is sometimes as much a luxury as the holiday itself.

The BBC tracked four large vessels around Wonsan, measuring approximately 50m, 55m, 60m and 80m. All four vessels repeatedly appeared around Kim's Wonsan villa this year.

The largest vessel showed the clearest activity, moving from the dock to the waters off the Kalma Peninsula, where it has been since July.

Two of the other vessels - 50m and 55m - were repeatedly seen until the end of August around Tae and Sin islands, close to Wonsan.

Satellite images also showed four smaller boats alongside the 50m vessel.

Satellite imagery expert Jeong Seong-hak said the smaller boats ferried people, fuel and supplies to the larger vessel, adding that small islands like Tae and Sin offered "secluded maritime retreats where privacy can be maintained away from public view".

The 60m vessel was repeatedly seen near Kim's Wonsan villa until as recently as last week.

Though North Korea has never publicly disclosed the vessels' official ownership, BBC's analysis of historical satellite imagery found a large vessel with the same distinctive characteristics in Wonsan in 2002, when Kim Jong Il ruled North Korea.

Former NBA star Dennis Rodman, who visited the North in 2013, told The Sun that he had spent much of his seven-day visit with Kim Jong Un around Wonsan, where they went jet-skiing and horse riding.

He also described a 60m vessel they used as a cross between a ferry and a Disney boat. It is not clear if this is the same 60m boat pictured in the above satellite imagery.

To most North Koreans, the life lived by the Kims and others who support the regime would seem not just extravagant but unimaginable. Especially because state propaganda is dedicated to presenting the "supreme leader" as a selfless man who always puts the nation first.

"Kim Jong Un is supposed to be a 'leader of the people'," Ri Jong Ho says, "yet he has four luxury vessels like these while ordinary people are struggling just to get one meal a day."

articles.title: In 2016, Mike Madden paid $520,000 for Muhammad Ali’s former Pennsylvania training camp; after investing another $1 million restoring its 13 log buildings, he reopened the six-acre site in 2019 as Fighter’s Heaven
articles.summary: In 2016, real estate investor Mike Madden paid $520,000 for Muhammad Ali’s former training camp in Pennsylvania, a property that had fallen into disrepair
articles.body: In 2016, real estate investor Mike Madden paid $520,000 for Muhammad Ali’s former training camp in Pennsylvania, a property that had fallen into disrepair after the boxing legend left it decades earlier. Madden subsequently invested another $1 million in restoring its 13 log structures, including the gymnasium and mosque, before reopening the six-acre site as Fighter’s Heaven in June 2019. According to Pennsylvania Heritage Magazine, the restoration sought to recreate the camp as it appeared when Ali trained there, turning a once-private sporting retreat into a place where visitors could explore the life and career of one of boxing’s most celebrated figures.The secluded camp where Ali prepared for his biggest fightsLocated near Orwigsburg in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, Fighter’s Heaven was established by Ali in 1972. The heavyweight champion wanted a secluded base where he could train away from the distractions of crowded gyms and the media attention that followed him. The idea came from Gene Kilroy, Ali’s business manager and a key figure in his professional career. Kilroy believed a remote training centre would give the boxer greater privacy while helping him control the costs of preparing for fights.Ali purchased approximately six acres of land after using a nearby property to prepare for earlier bouts. He then commissioned a collection of log buildings designed to function as a self-contained training community. The complex included a regulation-size boxing ring, Ali’s personal cabin, a kitchen and dining building, bunkhouses for sparring partners, a stable and a small mosque. A horse-drawn covered wagon, mobile homes for members of his team and other facilities also formed part of the camp.Ali trained there for many of his major fights between 1972 and 1981. These included bouts against Joe Frazier, George Foreman, Ken Norton and Floyd Patterson. The site also welcomed younger fighters, including Larry Holmes and Tim Witherspoon, who trained alongside or learned from Ali.The camp became known as Fighter’s Heaven in 1973, a name that reflected Ali’s affection for the secluded retreat and its importance to the boxing world.From abandoned property to a $520,000 purchaseAfter Ali stopped using the camp in 1981, the property entered a period of uncertainty. It remained largely vacant until 1997, when George Dillman, a karate instructor who had previously taught Ali, purchased it for $114,000. Dillman invested approximately $400,000 in repairs and operated the property as a martial arts school and a bed-and-breakfast establishment known as Butterfly & Bee. However, maintaining the complex eventually became difficult, and the property was put up for sale in 2002.Years later, Madden came across the former camp while searching online for information about Ali. The discovery stayed with him, and he travelled from California to Pennsylvania to see the property in person. Following Ali’s death on June 3, 2016, Madden decided to purchase the camp and preserve its history. He paid Dillman $520,000 in July 2016, according to Pennsylvania Heritage Magazine.Madden, the son of former Oakland Raiders coach and NFL broadcaster John Madden, had not initially developed a detailed commercial plan for the site. Instead, he saw an opportunity to protect a place associated with an important chapter in sporting history. “I think it’s a calling,” Madden said of the project in an interview published on Fighter’s Heaven’s website.Restoring 13 log structures to their former appearanceThe restoration required more than repairing a collection of ageing buildings. Madden wanted the site to resemble the camp Ali had used during the 1970s, rather than turning it into a modern museum detached from its original character. He spent approximately $1 million on the project, bringing craftsmen and former members of Ali’s circle into the process. Amish craftsmen helped restore several of the buildings, while historical photographs and personal recollections guided decisions about furnishings, equipment and the arrangement of the interiors.The gymnasium became a central feature of the restored site. Its boxing ring occupies the same location as Ali’s original ring, while photographs, fight posters and video displays document the boxer’s career.Ali’s personal cabin was also recreated using period-style furniture, with exhibits offering insight into how he lived during training camps. The kitchen retains its original long wooden dining table and gas stove, while a reproduction of the rules once associated with Ali’s aunt Coretta, who cooked at the camp, forms part of the display.The small mosque where Ali prayed was restored as well. Elsewhere, the property’s painted boulders preserve the names of boxers admired by Ali. His father, Cassius Clay Sr., painted the names on the rocks, giving them an additional connection to the family’s history.Reopening the camp to visitorsFighter’s Heaven held its grand reopening ceremony on June 1, 2019, attended by Madden, Kilroy and former heavyweight champion Tim Witherspoon. Public visits began later that month, allowing people to explore the buildings and learn about Ali’s training routines and life away from the ring. The restoration also received recognition from Pennsylvania’s State Historic Preservation Office. In November 2019, the office named Fighter’s Heaven among its Community Initiative Award recipients, recognising efforts to preserve historic places across the state.By March 2023, the camp’s official newsletter reported that thousands of visitors had toured the property since its reopening. The site had also hosted documentary crews working on productions about Ali, including Ken Burns’ documentary series Muhammad Ali and HBO’s What's My Name: Muhammad Ali.The newsletter also documented a heritage time capsule buried at the property in 2022, marking 50 years since Ali established the camp. Scheduled to be opened in 2072, the capsule contains photographs, articles, memorabilia and information about the restoration.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Huckabee condemns Israeli settlers’ attack on Washington Post photojournalist
articles.summary: Mike Huckabee, the U.S. Ambassador to Israel, condemned what he called a “vicious” and “cowardly” attack on a Washington Post photojournalist in the West Bank. The U.S. envoy shared a statement to the social platform X, calling for a full investigation into an attack by a group of Israeli settlers on Palestinians in Israel’s West…
articles.body:
Mike Huckabee, the U.S. Ambassador to Israel, condemned what he called a “vicious” and “cowardly” attack on a Washington Post photojournalist in the West Bank.

The U.S. envoy shared a statement to the social platform X, calling for a full investigation into an attack by a group of Israeli settlers on Palestinians in Israel’s West Bank, which injured Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine.

“Heidi is US Citizen, clear ID as journalist. Details of who under investigation, but those who attacked unarmed reporter should spend YRS in prison,” Huckabee wrote. “We have called for a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated in this.”

A video shared by the Post showed that Levine was wearing proper identification. In the clip, masked settlers appear to attack Levine, even after she was lying on the ground. Other journalists present came to her aid.

Huckabee has in the past referred to Israeli settlers who commit violence as “terrorists.” In Saturday’s statement, the former Arkansas governor referred to the attack as “an act of terror” and called the settlers “cowards.”

“Attacking a female photographer is despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards. Dishonorable act of senseless violence,” Huckabee wrote.

The attack on Levine was also condemned by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who said Friday that “those responsible will be held accountable.”

Settler violence is on the rise in Israel’s West Bank, with more than 1,600 attacks reported between January and August, according to the U.N. In September, Senate Democrats attempted to force a report on West Bank violence, but the vote was defeated 47-51. The measure would have stopped U.S. aid to Israel if the Trump administration did not produce a report on violence against U.S. citizens.

articles.title: Limoges Town Hall 'largely lost' after far-left rioters set historic building on fire amid French unrest
articles.summary: Rioters set fire to the historic Limoges Town Hall, collapsing its roof and destroying much of the landmark as France's protests rage on.
articles.body: A historic building in the French town of Limoges, about three hours south of Paris, has been "largely lost" after it was set on fire by rioters as demonstrations continue across France. The Limoges Town Hall was built in 1883, and was made a historic landmark in 1975. "The roof has collapsed onto lower floors, except the west wing, and two-thirds of the exterior has already disappeared," the local prefect, Maurice Barate, told the AFP news agency. MASSIVE FIRE DESTROYS 400-YEAR-OLD FOOD MARKET, LEAVING HISTORIC LANDMARK IN RUINS Barate called it "a deliberate act by hooligans," adding that it was a "catastrophe for heritage." The destruction came as far-left anti-government protests and violent clashes entered their fourth week in the European country over the cost of living. On Saturday, outgoing President Emmanuel Macron wrote on social media: "There is no place for violence in our republic." FRANCE EXPLODES AGAIN AS STUDENTS RIOT OVER EDUCATION "Those who have broken, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished," he added translated from French. "To the law enforcement forces, guarantors of the right to demonstrate, I express the support of the Nation. We will all stand united against the sowers of chaos, who seek only to bring down our institutions and prevent those who peacefully express their demands from doing so." Macron leaves office in six months. GRETA THUNBERG JOINS MASSIVE FRENCH STUDENT PROTESTS AS CARS BURN, POLICE FIRE TEAR GAS Around 400 people were arrested on Saturday, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, as more than a half million people took part in more than 100 marches across the country. Masked groups also attempted to break into city halls in Lille and Calais and a police station in Brest, the interior minister reported, along with violence in Rennes, Toulouse, Montpellier and Grenoble, among other cities. BEHIND FRANCE'S STUDENT RIOTS: COMMUNISTS, UNIONS AND A GLOBAL PROPAGANDA NETWORK Nuñez blamed the unrest on "extremely violent, radical far-left groups." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP While many of the protests were without violence, many have descended into riots. Police used tear gas and water cannons on Saturday to disperse violent groups in Paris, where people wearing hoods and masks threw fireworks and other objects at officers in the Place de la République.

articles.title: Northern Ireland health workers run out of patience with Stormont budget delay
articles.summary: The practical impact of Northern Ireland's budget delay seemed relatively muted until earlier this week when hospital doctors announced two strikes.
articles.body:
The Northern Ireland Executive is now seven months into the financial year without a budget.

One of the remarkable things about this situation is the relatively muted practical impacts.

Public sector managers have adapted to emergency budget procedures; the money still flows, services are delivered, wages are paid.

But this week real consequences began to emerge as hospital doctors ran out of patience and announced two strikes next month .

The lack of a Stormont budget means the doctors cannot be given the 3.5% pay uplift which was recommended by an independent body and accepted by the health minister.

Hospital doctors to strike as pay dispute continues

Resident doctors in England accept pay deal and end strikes

Divided executive 'speaking as one' on budget, says finance minister

"I don't know long you'd like us to wait?" said Clodagh Corrigan from the doctors' union, the British Medical Association (BMA).

The BMA met the health minister two weeks ago, and Corrigan said they were told that there will be no pay rise before Christmas "if at all".

In response resident doctors will hold a 24-hour walk out on Friday 20 November while consultants and specialists will operate a much-reduced service on the following Monday.

The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has opened a ballot for industrial action for the same reasons as the doctors.

"It is despicable that, year after year, nursing staff in Northern Ireland are forced to fight for a pay award that colleagues elsewhere in the UK receive as a matter of course," said Professor Rita Devlin, executive director of the RCN in Northern Ireland.

"Would governments in England, Scotland or Wales allow their health service staff to go indefinitely without a pay award? The answer is no.

"So why is Northern Ireland expected to accept this?"

Health Minister Robbie Butler has attempted to strike a conciliatory note while acknowledging there will be no movement without a budget deal.

"I remain committed to implementing this year's pay award but unfortunately, I am currently unable to do so in the absence of a sufficient budget being agreed for my department," he said.

There is no budget because of a consensus among the executive parties that the operation of the UK's devolution funding formula now leaves them so short that they cannot produce a workable financial plan.

The UK government has conceded that more funding is necessary and has offered an additional £1.5bn over the next three years , with a first tranche of £525m to be paid this year.

The Stormont parties say this is nowhere near enough.

'Budget settlement must include pay uplifts'

On Tuesday, Finance Minister John O'Dowd laid out his position in the assembly.

"Pressures across departments in the current financial year are around £1.6bn. The offer that is currently on the table is around £525m.

"Public sector pay alone is £500m or thereabouts, and any settlement or agreement has to include money for pay uplifts for teachers, nurses and other public-sector workers."

Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant has reacted with exasperation.

"You cannot keep overspending willy-nilly and not expect consequences from that. It's just irresponsible," he told the BBC.

He held a virtual meeting with Stormont ministers on Friday. There was no sign of agreement.

More discussions will be held next week.

Bryant has suggested the absolute deadline for reaching a deal is January because at that point the money available to spend under the emergency arrangements will run out.

A deal will need to be reached much sooner than that if strikes are to be avoided.

articles.title: Iran says two tankers catch fire after hitting mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: The vessels, each carrying about two million barrels of crude oil, used an unauthorised route, the IRGC says.
articles.body:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said two oil tankers, each carrying about two million barrels of crude oil, caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

The first tanker hit a mine, triggering an explosion and a “fierce fire”, the IRGC said on Saturday, while the second tanker hit a mine that engulfed it “in a massive blaze”, Iran’s official IRNA news agency reported.

Information about the ships’ names or the origin of their cargo was not immediately available.

IRNA said the vessels had switched off their positioning and radar systems and tried to use a route not authorised by Iran.

The IRGC also claimed that while one tanker tried to cross the waterway “with US support”, the second vessel was left immobilised.

Iran seized control of the Strait of Hormuz after the US-Israeli war on the country began in late February. Tehran has since demanded that all ships seek its authorisation before transiting. About one-fifth of global oil consumption transited the waterway before the war.

This week, IRGC naval commander Rear Admiral Ali Azmaei warned that any vessel that deactivated its navigation systems would be considered “hostile”.

The United States has imposed its own naval counter-blockade on Iranian oil exports.

Iran’s army earlier said that two tankers caught fire on Thursday and Friday in Tehran’s “prohibited zone” in the Gulf of Oman.

Maritime monitors also reported two tankers struck in Gulf waters off Saudi Arabia on Friday.

Last Sunday, six vessels were attacked in or near the Strait of Hormuz, the most in a single day since the war began, according to security firm Vanguard, the International Maritime Organization and the UK maritime agency UKMTO.

Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past two weeks, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions imposed last month.

Nearly 20.8 million barrels of oil passed through on October 8, but only 2.9 million on October 11, according to Kpler data.

The disruption has pushed up global energy prices and inflation.

US President Donald Trump has explicitly ruled out using a nuclear weapon against Iran. “I wouldn’t use nuclear,” he told the Newsmax news site in an interview on Thursday.

Trump said that he was also not considering putting troops on the ground in Iran. “No, I don’t see that, I don’t see it,” he said, adding he believes a deal to end the war will be reached after the November 3 US midterm elections.

articles.body: Restrictions on Ukraine’s military use of SpaceX’s Starshield, a militarised version of Starlink, appear to be deliberate and not the result of any technical problems, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday.Speed limitations on the internet network remain in place across Ukraine, resulting in a significant slowing down of connections, Zelenskyy said in audio messages to reporters on WhatsApp. Ukraine sent vehicles connected to Starshield to Europe to conduct speed checks and found they operated normally, Zelenskyy said. The restrictions “are on the territory of Ukraine –– so it is a planned operation,” he said.US President Donald Trump said Friday that he didn’t order any limitations on Ukraine’s access to the system and didn’t think SpaceX Chairman Elon Musk had either. Musk on Wednesday said “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately” the president. Ukraine depends on Starshield to help its air defences intercept jet-powered drones that Russia is firing at Kyiv and other cities, as well as to target artillery strikes.BloombergYou use AI every day. articles.body: Cairo: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday Egypt would take any measures necessary to defend Saudi Arabia if asked, amid escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom, and parliament announced an emergency session on Sunday. “It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi, its security or stability to be harmed,” Sisi said at a graduation ceremony at Egyptian Military Academy. He said Egypt was not seeking to attack anyone, but was prepared to act in defence.Sisi said Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who visited Sisi on Sept 15,Saudi says intercepted drones over RiyadhSaudi Arabia said Saturday it had intercepted four drones, including over the capital Riyadh, as the country comes under repeated fire from Houthis. articles.title: Deaths and injuries reported in incident at military base in Alberta
articles.summary: EDMONTON, Alberta — Canada’s defense minister said Saturday that people were killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire.
articles.body: EDMONTON, Alberta — Canada’s defense minister said Saturday that people were killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire. “I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base,” Defense Minister David McGuinty said. McGuinty did not provide casualty figures or details about what caused the incident. He said the Royal Canadian Mounted Police were involved in the investigation and described the situation as “very, very active and delicate.” The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers were called shortly after 4 p.m. Saturday following reports of a fire in a training area at the base. The Canadian Armed Forces and federal, provincial and local authorities were coordinating the emergency response, he said. The nearby community of Wainwright was providing hospital and firefighting support. The Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire had crossed the military base’s perimeter fence and was spreading rapidly in high winds. Firefighters from multiple jurisdictions were responding, and no evacuation order was in effect. Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said his province was sending assistance to Alberta but did not specify what resources were being deployed. “Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected,” Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier in a social media post. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith described the fire as “significant and tragic” and said it was affecting many military personnel. Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, about 112 miles southeast of Edmonton, is one of Canada’s busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations. It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides military training. McGuinty said authorities were still working to determine what happened and expected to provide further information. Carney said the federal government was working closely with Alberta officials and local authorities. He said he and Smith were in close contact, as were their ministers and officials. Smith thanked first responders and those providing care and support to those affected. Canadian Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre said he had spoken with Carney and the defense minister to offer support to those affected by the fire. “Pray for Wainwright, everyone,” Poilievre said in a social media post. He urged people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders. Neither Carney nor Smith provided details about what caused the fire or whether anyone was injured. The fire disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday’s referendum on whether Alberta should begin a process that could lead to independence from Canada. Elections Alberta said two polling locations, in Lloydminster and Vermilion, closed early Saturday and the ballots were transported securely.

articles.title: Search continues for 11 missing after boat sank off Mexico’s Baja coast
articles.summary: Some of 16 survivors treated for suspected shark bites, US coastguard says.
articles.body:
The search continues for 11 people still missing after a boat capsized off Mexico’s Baja California coast on Friday, as multiple survivors have been treated for suspected shark bites, according to the US coastguard.

“Several of the individuals rescued were suffering from severe injuries consistent with shark bites, and the Coast Guard provided life-saving first aid while en route [to] San Diego,” the coastguard said in a statement on Saturday.

Sixteen Mexican nationals were rescued on Friday. Survivors told officials there were 27 people on board.

The coastguard and US Navy used multiple aircraft and boats, along with assistance from the Mexican Navy, to search the area for the remaining passengers. An additional helicopter will be deployed later on Saturday, according to the coastguard.

A Mayday call was transmitted from someone on the boat at about 1am on Friday, coastguard Lieutenant Santiago Tamburini said on the day.

A rescue helicopter reached the site about two hours later. It took about 90 minutes for the crew, which included a rescue swimmer, to pull the 16 people from the water, he added.

The boat went down about 225km (140 miles) west of Ensenada, Mexico, an area popular with fishing and leisure boats, but that is also frequented by smugglers.

Although the incident did not happen in US waters, coastguard official Charlie Valor said on Saturday they “were able to help, and that’s why we launched our assets”.

Fatal attempts to transport refugees and migrants from Mexico to the US have occurred in the past.

In May 2025, at least three people died when a boat flipped off the coast about 56km (35 miles) north of the US-Mexico border.

In 2023, eight people were killed in one of the deadliest maritime smuggling accidents off the US coast, when two boats approached a San Diego beach in heavy fog, and one capsized in the surf.

articles.title: Deadly fire breaks out after ‘serious incident’ at Canada military base
articles.summary: A major fire caused deaths and injuries at one of Canada’s busiest military bases on Saturday, sparked by an unspecified “serious incident,” with authorities still working to contain the blaze.
articles.body: A major fire caused deaths and injuries at one of Canada’s busiest military bases on Saturday, sparked by an unspecified “serious incident,” with authorities still working to contain the blaze. The fire began at the base in Wainwright, a town in eastern Alberta province, according to officials, and “spread rapidly due to high winds,” said the municipal district in a Facebook post Saturday evening. A call for assistance came around 4 p.m., according to the Wainwright Royal Canadian Mounted Police. Defense Minister David McGuinty said in a video statement “that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incident on the base.” He did not provide details about the number of casualties or what caused the initial blaze, but called it an “active and delicate situation.” The fire is still “underway on the ground,” and an investigation will be launched soon, he added. CFB Wainwright, located about 210 kilometers (130 miles) southeast of provincial capital Edmonton, is one of the country’s busiest Army bases, according to a government website. It houses the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre; it’s also a training ground for Army field force units based in Edmonton. Prime Minister Mark Carney confirmed the fire had stemmed from “a serious incident,” without specifying details. CNN has reached out to the military base, the Wainwright fire department, the Alberta premier’s office, and the municipal district for more details. The Canadian Armed Forces, the federal government, provincial and local authorities are cooperating “to mobilize all necessary support, and working through the details of what actually occurred,” McGuinty said. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith called the disaster “significant and tragic,” saying it was “affecting many of our brave military personnel.” No evacuation order has been issued. Authorities have asked residents to avoid the incident area, keep roads clear, and avoid visiting the Wainwright Health Center except for critical medical needs. “I cannot recall such an incident in my short time for sure as a minister … I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory,” McGuinty said in the video statement, responding to a journalist’s question. Opposition leader Pierre Poilievre also wrote in a post that he had spoken to McGuinty and Carney about the fire, thanked emergency responders, and added: “Pray for Wainwright, everyone.” This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Kolkata stampede: Puja secretary among 7 held; SIT to probe crowd lapses, culpable homicide case filed
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Seven people, including the secretary and vice-president of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity, have been arrested in connection with the
articles.body: KOLKATA: Seven people, including the secretary and vice-president of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity, have been arrested in connection with the stampede at the Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata that left 19 people dead and 25 hospitalised.The state government has constituted a special investigation team (SIT) to probe the tragedy, with investigators examining possible lapses in crowd management and security arrangements.Those arrested include Raj Kumar Sewda, alias Raja (48), the puja committee's secretary, and Santanu Dubey (55), its vice-president. The other accused are Biplab Mukherjee, alias Joy (48), who was involved in constructing the bamboo structure at the pandal; Koushik Saha (53), who was responsible for crowd control and checking VIP passes; Pintu Dey (51), who was engaged in crowd management; and private security in-charges Suman Chakraborty (30) and Rajesh Pal (29).Kolkata Police have registered a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the stampede, an officer said. The case was registered at Girish Park police station under Sections 105, 110 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the organisers and others.A forensic team visited the site, while police began questioning puja committee members, security personnel and police officers to establish the sequence of events leading to the stampede.West Bengal minister Umesh Rai, who visited Calcutta Medical College and Hospital to meet the injured, said the SIT would examine the circumstances of the incident and identify those responsible for any negligence.“This is a very tragic accident. The chief minister had called for action against those responsible yesterday. We are forming an SIT, which will investigate the entire incident and the circumstances in which it occurred,” Rai said.Rain, overcrowding and entry-exit movement under scannerGiving a preliminary account of the incident, Rai said the pandal had witnessed heavy footfall over the past several days. When it began raining, a large number of visitors rushed inside to take shelter, while those already inside struggled to get out.The situation worsened as people continued entering from one side even as others attempted to leave through the other, he said. The pandal's dark interiors, part of its themed setup, added to the difficulties, though Rai said darkness alone was not responsible for the stampede.“When it started raining, people inside could not leave the pandal, while a large number of people continued to enter from behind. The stampede occurred at that point,” he said.Rai alleged that the puja organisers and the security agency responsible for crowd management had failed to discharge their duties. The SIT will investigate the alleged lapses, and strict action will be taken against anyone found responsible for negligence, he said.Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said preliminary information received from the assistant commissioner of police present at the spot suggested that an announcement made by a private security agency and the blowing of whistles may have triggered the incident.Adhikari said puja committee members and security agency personnel had been detained for questioning. He assured that the investigation would be conducted transparently and that the government would provide assistance to the affected families.“As a chief minister, I can't give a statement before the investigation is over, but I assure that proper investigation will be done with full transparency. The puja committee members and the security agencies have been detained. All kind of support will be provided to all families. This is a very, very sad incident,” he said.Minister appeals against politicising tragedyRai appealed to political parties to refrain from politicising the incident, saying the immediate priority should be to assist the injured and support the families of those who died.“Those inclined toward politics will find an opportunity to play politics anywhere; however, I believe that in such adverse circumstances, the most significant humanitarian gesture is to stand by those who are injured and the families who have lost their loved ones. It would be far better to keep politics out of this,” he said.The minister also urged Durga Puja organisers across West Bengal to review crowd management arrangements, increase the number of entry and exit gates and ensure adequate lighting, particularly at crowded pandals with poorly lit interiors.With celebrations scheduled to continue over the next three to four days, he asked organisers to take immediate steps to prevent overcrowding and avoid similar incidents.“We want Durga Puja to be celebrated and for people to enjoy themselves, but it is essential that no accidents occur. The organisers of the Durga Puja celebrations must keep this in mind,” he said.Political programmes cancelledWest Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya also provided an update on the patient reported to be critical, saying doctors were hopeful of recovery. The patient was being shifted to a private hospital, with the medical expenses to be covered, he said.Bhattacharya announced that Union home minister Amit Shah's scheduled programmes in West Bengal on Sunday had been cancelled following the tragedy. Nitin Nabin's planned visit to the state was also called off.Adhikari announced the cancellation of all events scheduled for Sunday in view of the incident.The investigation is expected to examine the movement of visitors inside the pandal, the arrangements for entry and exit, the role of the organisers and private security personnel, and the circumstances surrounding the announcement and whistles before the stampede.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news.
